briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 launch intensifies frontier race as US export controls tighten on advanced chips

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race accelerates with multiple frontier model releases this month. Geopolitical tensions drive compute restrictions while safety concerns mount over production deployments. Funding remains robust across major labs and infrastructure providers.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4 with multimodal reasoning gains. Anthropic launched Claude 4 Opus. Google DeepMind deployed Gemini 3. Meta open-sourced Llama 4. xAI and DeepSeek announced new reasoning models this week. Competition centers on agentic capabilities.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. Regulators in EU and US advance mandatory red-teaming rules. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent and IoT environments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA shipped next-gen Blackwell clusters to Microsoft and Oracle. TSMC expanded Arizona fabs for AI chips. Saudi Arabia announced $40B data center investment tied to US tech partners. Power constraints delay several hyperscale projects.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will export controls on advanced semiconductors meaningfully slow Chinese frontier model progress by end of 2027?
